newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: LEADS ON BIG CANNABIS HAUL UP IN SMOKE
Mystery surrounds the arrival in Australia of more than five-tonnes of compressed cannabis, imported by sea from Cambodia.
The seizure was made on November 13, but has been kept secret until now because Federal Police were waiting for someone to claim the container of jute the drugs were concealed in.
It's one of the biggest seizures of drugs the Customs service has ever made, with a street value of over A$50 million. The matter is still being investigated, both here and overseas.
JEWELLER REMANDED OVER MELBOURNE SHOOTINGS
A Melbourne jeweller has been remanded in custody to appear in April next year over the murder of another jeweller and his son yesterday.
Manuel Adjian, 41, of Endeavour Hills, was charged with the murder of Lean Thoeun Pin 49, his son Virayuth Pin, 21, and the attempted murder of Siving Pun, 44.
During the brief court hearing, Magistrate Pat Street was told Adjian, also a jeweller, entered the Pun's gem dealership intending to make part payment of a debt.
An argument is believed to have taken place and it's alleged Adjian then pulled out a handgun, firing nine shots.
PENSIONERS' INTEREST RATES TO FALL
The Federal Government has reduced the interest rates on pensioners' savings accounts.
The so-called deeming rate will fall from five to four per cent on investments of up to 50-thousand dollars for a pensioner couple, and from seven to six per cent on amounts above this.
Social Security Minister, Jocelyn Newman, says the move is in-line with the recent falls in official interest rates and will be the last change to the deeming rates for some time.
Some of the banks wanted to reduce the deeming rates by larger amounts but were rebuffed by the Government.
The lower rates will apply from January the 23rd next year.
SYDNEY AIRPORT IN OLYMPIC EXPANSION

The 2000 Olympics have sparked a major building expansion of Sydney Airport. A$56 million worth of new roads are to be built along with ten new arrival gates, and a hotel on top of the international terminal.
GOVERNMENT PLANS AIRLINE RATINGS
Federal Transport Minister, John Sharp, says it's remarkable that Australia gives ratings to hotels, caravan parks and restaurants, but doesn't rate airlines.

Sharp says a move to rate the safety levels of individual airlines is being considered. His comments came as he announced the Government will next year issue monthly reports naming airlines with serious safety problems.
Sharp says the move's part of measures to improve information given to consumers about the airlines they use, and the types of planes they fly in.
Other measures include a telephone information service and pamphlets on aircraft types.
HOWARD TREADS SOFTLY ON REPUBLIC
Prime Minister, John Howard, says the Government will have a look at a proposal on the republic put forward by the Opposition but says the Government won't be rushed into a decision.
The Opposition has proposed a plebiscite next year, with a referendum held after a joint parliamentary inquiry.
Howard says he's not trying to bury the issue, but believes it should be given calm consideration.
GOVERNMENT DEFENDS RACISM SILENCE
Senator Nick Minchin has denied the Federal Government has its head in the sand over the racism debate.
Minchin is representing the Prime Minister at a national Ethnic Communities Council of Australia conference in Adelaide.
In his opening address, the President of the South Australian council, Randolph Alwis, called on politicians to take a stand against political opportunists who make racist comments.
Alwis says politicians who ignore statements such as those made by Federal Independent MP, Pauline Hanson, can be seen as condoning their views.
But Senator Minchin rejected criticism of the Government's handling of the debate.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
